title: Hadith visual world
status: Operational art direction derived from the user-approved ten-image shortlist. The synthesis and palette are design interpretations, not separately approved new images.
userIntent: Use the shortlisted landscapes as shared visual DNA for future images. Do not treat this as approval of daily rotation, per-hadith assignment or ten selectable scene skins.
premise: An imagined warm land of terraced green valleys, spring-fed stone gardens, flourishing oases and ancient sculptural trees. Each view feels like a comfortable place to pause, with room to discover something extraordinary.
interpretation: Warmth comes from light, living vegetation and tactile materials; it does not require an orange sunset in every image.
Shelter and distance work together: a nearby canopy, garden edge or stone opening frames an inviting view.
The selected set permits both lush abundance and open dunes. Water and flowers are recurring motifs, not mandatory props.
Wonder comes from distinctive landforms, ancient trees, luminous minerals or generous natural scale. Keep one dominant extraordinary feature per scene.
No coastal scene appears in the selected ten. Keep beaches secondary for this direction; this is not a permanent ban on coastlines.
The images share richly observed, painterly naturalism and deep spatial layers. Avoid generic fantasy illustration or flat decorative clip art.

regions.name: Terraced valleys
regions.character: Broad cultivated curves, lush rounded limestone hills, emerald fields, red-earth paths and sparse vertical palm accents. Open, rhythmic and spacious.
regions.transition: Terraces follow valley contours; small channels lead toward the garden basins below.
regions.avoid: Cold alpine silhouettes; putting a palm in every corner; forcing a central river into every view.

regions.name: Gardens of stone and water
regions.character: Warm sandstone and ivory limestone shelter clear jade springs. An occasional opalescent outcrop or sunlit opening supplies the wonder. Vines and flowers soften mineral edges.
regions.transition: A spring can emerge beneath a limestone opening, flow across mineral shelves and enter a sheltered canyon.
regions.avoid: Combining cave, opal mountain, enormous waterfall and palace in one image; icy crystals or dark enclosed caverns.

regions.name: Oasis margins and dunes
regions.character: Rose-gold earthen channels, palms and flowering garden edges gradually give way to apricot dunes, rounded granite, acacias and breathing room.
regions.transition: Irrigated gardens become sparse shade groves and then soft open dunes; let the planting thin naturally.
regions.avoid: A dense rainforest pasted onto sand; oppressive heat, dust storms, dead trees or empty threatening wilderness.

regions.name: Ancient canopy groves
regions.character: Monumental copper trunks or umbrella crowns, pale stone, warm grassy paths and small flowering pockets. The tree silhouette defines the place.
regions.transition: Dry garden plateaus support broad sculptural canopies, with denser shade toward the valley margins.
regions.avoid: Treating baobabs and dragon trees as interchangeable; crowding both signature forms into every grove.

night.principle: Night is a lighting state within this same world, not a separate cold biome. Preserve a recognisable place when creating a day/night pair.
night.colors: Deep teal and green shadows, creamy flowers, restrained amber pools of light. Keep paths and foliage readable.
night.architecture: Occasional modest open timber pavilions, low stone steps and warm lanterns. Architecture supports the garden; it is not the subject of every scene.
night.avoid: A global orange filter, icy blue moonlight, black voids, neon glow or many competing light sources.

invariants: The atmosphere is warm, pleasant, sheltered and unhurried.
Use softly shaped or weathered terrain with tangible stone, bark, leaf and water textures.
Use verdant greens with warm mineral colours. Cooler jade water and teal shadows provide relief.
Compose from somewhere the viewer could comfortably pause. Offer a nearby resting place for the eye and a clear route into depth.
Use rich detail in selected areas and broad quiet areas elsewhere. Do not make every surface equally busy.
Keep one dominant landform and one botanical signature. Additional elements support them.
Vary camera height, framing and land/water balance across the collection. Avoid repeating the same river-between-two-trees template.
Use a consistent refined oil-and-gouache painterly naturalism, soft atmospheric distance and tactile foreground detail.
Keep the artistic world separate from hadith meaning: no depiction of narrated events and no claim that a scene shows Jannah or al-Firdaws.
Hadith wording remains outside the generated artwork and must not be rewritten or turned into decorative image text.

palette.note: Proposed art-direction swatches, visually interpreted from the anchors; not measured pixel samples or validated UI colours.

swatches.name: Warm limestone
swatches.role: Rock highlights and sunlit quiet areas

imageRoles.welcome: An immersive wide view with a strong recognisable silhouette, layered depth and one quiet area. Prepare framing for the actual desktop and phone containers; do not assume a single crop will preserve the subject.
imageRoles.readingStrip: A close detail or intentionally composed panoramic fragment from the same world. Prefer a terrace curve, canopy edge, stone ledge or water surface. Fewer competing focal points and restrained contrast. Do not shrink a dense hero into a narrow strip.
imageRoles.nightCompanion: Edit the approved day scene: preserve landmarks, geometry, planting and camera position; change lighting and the minimum supporting light sources.
imageRoles.ui: Retain the approved comfortable 21px reading size. Artwork stays separate from the hadith text. Existing accessible reader colours remain until a specific palette change is evaluated. This guide does not introduce animation or rotation.

avoid: Cold dread, snow, harsh wind, barren winter branches and icy light
Repeated generic island verandas, resort furniture and postcard beaches as the default
Aggressive cliffs, crashing waves, threatening dark tunnels and precarious viewpoints
Overcrowding all regional motifs into one scene or flattening distinctive plants into generic tropical foliage
Uniform sunset orange, fluorescent green, plastic textures, excessive bloom and sharp neon crystals
People, animals, religious figures, calligraphy, lettering, logos and UI baked into generated artwork under the current landscape-only brief
generationWorkflow: Read this guide and inspect the relevant selected original images before writing a new prompt.
Choose one region, one image role, one lighting state, one primary landform and one botanical signature.
Select two or three relevant anchors: one for landform and composition, one for light and planting, and optionally one for material. State each reference role explicitly.
Use the common prompt plus a scene-specific brief. Do not concatenate every motif or the original country prompts.
Keep lighting, materials, painterly rendering and emotional tone consistent while varying geography and composition.
Generate with the built-in image tool, inspect the result, then test the intended phone and desktop crops before adoption.
For day/night pairs, edit the approved day image to retain the same place.
Keep original outputs, exact prompts, anchor IDs, reference roles, image role and tool provenance with each accepted asset. Make lighter delivery copies as needed.
Treat new outputs as candidates. Reuse the ten approved anchors until the user explicitly promotes new work into the reference set.
reviewQuestions: Would this feel like a pleasant place to pause?
Does it belong beside the chosen references through light, material and painting style?
Can its defining landform or tree silhouette be recognised quickly?
Is there breathing room, including in the intended reading-strip crop?
Does it add a distinct view rather than repeat a previous composition?
Are wonder and lushness controlled rather than crowded?
Does the night version remain welcoming and geographically consistent?
Is all hadith wording outside the image and untouched?
basePrompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Create an original landscape for the Hadith reader visual world, Gardens of Warm Light. An imagined warm land of terraced valleys, sheltered mineral springs, oasis margins and ancient sculptural canopies. Use the supplied anchor images in their stated reference roles. Refined oil-and-gouache painterly naturalism, tactile stone and bark, richly observed foliage, soft atmospheric depth. The scene feels pleasant, sheltered and quietly extraordinary. Choose one dominant landform and one botanical signature; preserve breathing room. Warm mineral colours and living greens, relieved by jade water or deep teal shadow when relevant. Warmth need not mean sunset or an orange wash. Use one restrained extraordinary feature at most. This is an imagined reading environment, not a depiction of a hadith event or the actual appearance of Jannah. No figures, animals, lettering, calligraphy, logos or UI. Avoid cold dread, icy light, resort clichés, neon effects and repetitive centred-river compositions. Follow the scene, lighting, composition and delivery-role instructions below.
